transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Welcome to broadband customer technical support. My name is Craig. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Craig. I am calling in absolute terror about my mother's landline and broadband. My eighty-nine-year-old mother lives alone and wears an emergency red pendant alarm around her neck that dials out to social services through the landline telephone socket. Ever since S-Net upgraded our broadband connection three days ago, the emergency alarm base unit has been screeching, flashing red fault lights, and completely failing to connect calls!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can look into the telephone line diagnostics for you. Can you provide the account customer reference number and the broadband Hub serial number from the label?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The account reference is ACC-994821 and the Hub serial number is SN-HUB5-882049.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that brings up the line profile on my screen. What is the landline telephone number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The phone number is 0141 496 0882. Craig, this morning my mother had a severe dizzy spell, collapsed onto the kitchen floor, and pressed her emergency pendant button in sheer panic! But instead of connecting to the medical emergency operator, the alarm base station made a violent screeching noise and gave an engaged tone! She was lying helpless on the cold floor for nearly an hour before a neighbour heard her tapping on the wall! If she had suffered a major stroke or cardiac arrest, she could have died on that floor because S-Net's broadband disabled her lifeline! This is a matter of life and death!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: VDSL high-speed broadband signals transmit high frequencies up to seventeen megahertz along copper telephone lines, which generate acoustic audible hum if unseparated from standard voice frequencies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Craig, please understand that my mother could have died! We need to make sure this emergency medical alarm works reliably right this minute!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So if I understand correctly, your mother's emergency social alarm pendant unit is failing to connect emergency dispatch calls due to severe broadband noise interference on the shared landline socket following the broadband service upgrade. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happened. The medical unit is a Tunstall Lifeline VI social alarm.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net is strictly an internet service provider; medical pendant alarms and warden-call equipment are managed by private care providers and local councils, so S-Net holds zero liability or responsibility for social alarm hardware.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The alarm unit worked perfectly for four years until S-Net activated this new broadband line! The broadband frequencies are leaking into the phone socket! You cannot just wash your hands of it!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am initiating a remote loop resistance and line capacitance test on the copper pair from the local exchange.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What do the electrical line test results indicate?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The automated line test reports an impedance imbalance and high radio frequency bleed across the analogue lower band.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What causes that radio frequency bleed on the line?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Standard plug-in microfilter dongles often suffer capacitive degradation, allowing VDSL high frequencies to saturate the analogue modem in the alarm base unit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the alarm modem is being blinded by broadband noise whenever the router transmits data?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The VDSL transmission tones flood the dial tone detection frequency, preventing the alarm dialer from recognizing the line signal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why the alarm unit was screeching and giving an engaged signal when my mother pressed her button!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fitting a hardwired Openreach interstitial filtered master socket faceplate isolates high-frequency broadband signals completely from the analogue telephone circuits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that hardwired faceplate have separate dedicated ports for the router and the medical alarm?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: An Openreach Master Socket 5C faceplate features an isolated top RJ11 port for the VDSL router and a bottom filtered BS6312 socket for analogue telecare devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you book an engineer to come out and install that filtered faceplate immediately?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can schedule an Openreach special fault engineer appointment under vulnerable telecare priority.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When is the earliest possible appointment slot available?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The earliest available emergency telecare engineering appointment is tomorrow morning between eight o'clock and one o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning between eight and one works perfectly. I will stay at my mother's flat to let the engineer in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The booking reference for the telecare socket upgrade is ENG-883912.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have written down ENG-883912.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The engineer will replace the front plate of the master socket and verify signal separation with a hand-held golden modem tester.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What should we do tonight to keep my mother safe until the engineer arrives tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Unplugging the grey broadband DSL cable from the wall socket tonight restores pure analogue copper continuity for the alarm dialer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So if we disconnect the router until tomorrow, the pendant alarm will work normally without interference?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously with the router powered off, zero high-frequency modulation exists on the copper pair to disrupt analogue telecare calls.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will unplug the router immediately so my mother's alarm is fully operational tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check the electrical ring main circuit near the socket to ensure no switch-mode chargers are generating electromagnetic noise.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There are no mobile phone chargers near the master socket; only the Tunstall base unit is plugged in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us check the REN loading factor on the telephone line to make sure total connected ringer equivalence remains under four.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Only the Tunstall unit and one corded telephone are plugged in, so REN is around two.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Total REN load of two leaves adequate electrical ringing current for social alarm triggering.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is good to know.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us review the priority flags on the customer account to add a permanent Telecare User designation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please add that flag so all future support agents know this line has life-critical equipment.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The telecare safety tag prevents automated network re-profiles from disrupting line stability.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That provides great reassurance.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us confirm the contact telephone number for the Openreach engineer to send arrival text notifications tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The best mobile contact number is my mobile: 07700 900512.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have set 07700 900512 as the primary mobile for Openreach engineer tracking and arrival alerts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will the engineer phone thirty minutes prior to arrival?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The engineer sends an SMS message upon dispatch from the previous job and places a direct phone call approximately twenty minutes before arrival.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will give me plenty of time to be at the door.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The engineer will also inspect the external drop-wire and junction box to ensure no corrosion degrades copper conductivity.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The external drop-wire was replaced two years ago and looks brand new.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Clean external wiring ensures maximum noise rejection across all frequencies.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am glad we are getting the master socket properly filtered.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let us also check whether the alarm base unit battery backup is holding a charge in case of mains power failure.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The Tunstall unit green battery light is on and shows healthy battery condition.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to reconfirm, the telecare equipment installed is the Tunstall Lifeline VI social alarm base unit under appointment ENG-883912.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, Tunstall Lifeline VI under ENG-883912. That is correct.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The engineer work order explicitly notes telecare model Tunstall Lifeline VI and master socket faceplate installation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Craig, that covers the booking details.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, Craig, once the engineer finishes tomorrow, how do we properly trigger a test alarm call to verify dispatch without...

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The engineer will test it. Have a good day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Craig? He disconnected while I was asking how to test the alarm! Unbelievable!
